one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-04. Scheduled: Uber Q3 2026 results expected ~Nov 3-4 (not yet confirmed; TipRanks lists Nov 3) - guidance was GB $58.25-60.25B, Non-GAAP EPS $0.84-0.88, adj. EBITDA $2.86-2.96B; Uber has beaten the high end of GB guidance repeatedly but the stock fell ~5% on Q2 on soft guide, so the reaction is two-sided. Tesla Q3 results (~late Oct) will carry Cybercab/robotaxi commentary - the Austin Cybercab fleet is small (45 at launch, active fleet fell back to ~8 per Electrek 9/22), so headline risk exceeds real volume risk. Waymo city launches continue (Kalshi priced Las Vegas at 82c on 9/2) - each launch has been a mild negative headline. Lyft (Q3 guide reaffirmed 9/9) and DoorDash likely report just after the window. The CA ballot fight was settled via SB 623, so the Nov 3 election is not a catalyst. Stock is near its 52-week low after a -29.5% year; no strong momentum or reversal edge. I keep a near-symmetric distribution centred slightly above spot (median ~$69.9) with ~11% one-month sigma (35%/3.5 = 10%, bumped for earnings in window).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (17x on ~$4.80 NTM Non-GAAP EPS at Oct-2027 = $82), EV/FCF (15x on ~$10.5B FCF after SBC = ~$80) and EV/adj. EBITDA (10.5x on ~$15.9B NTM adj. EBITDA = ~$85); weights 40/35/25 give ~$82.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (Oct-2027 to Oct-2028) Non-GAAP EPS ~$4.80 x 17.0x

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY26 EPS; cross-checked vs Q2 actual $0.81 and Q3 guide $0.84-0.88 (sources 1,2).

FY27 ~$4.20 (+25%, below Q3 guided 28-35% YoY growth to allow for AV investment and Brazil supply spend) and FY28 ~$5.00 (+19%); NTM at Oct-27 = 0.25*4.20+0.75*5.00. Q2 buybacks cut diluted shares ~4% YoY (source 2).

Inside core-profitable peer range 8.0-28.8x, roughly at the 7-peer core median 17.7x. No premium: Uber's faster EPS growth than BKNG/EXPE is offset by an unresolved AV-disintermediation risk (Waymo going direct in Austin/Atlanta from Jan-2028, source 9) that I cannot argue away within 12 months.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF after SBC ~$10.5B x 15x EV/FCF = $157B EV; less net debt ~$4.7B, plus non-DH listed stakes ~$8B; /2.0B shares

inputs_detail.input: NTM FCF after SBC at Oct-2027
inputs_detail.derivation: TTM FCF $10.1B grown ~20% (in line with GB growth 18-22% and EBITDA growth 33%) to ~$12.5B, less ~$2.0B SBC.

Uber trades at 14.2x EV/TTM FCF today (source 3); Wolfe used 20x 'in line with gig/OTA leaders' in Sep-2025 (source 10) before the AV de-rating; BKNG/EXPE trade ~10-12x EBITDA. 15x on post-SBC FCF is a modest discount to that 20x and near today's multiple.
Cash $5.4B vs debt $12.7B per Q2 release; DH acquisition (~$9B for remaining ~63% at EUR41.50) treated as NPV-neutral: debt added offsets value acquired.
Investments marked $12.5B at Q2 incl. ~$4B DH economic interest; ~$8B ex-DH, mostly listed.
2.05B diluted at Q2, 2.04B outstanding now; buybacks continue (~$16B authorization) but slower while funding DH.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM adj. EBITDA at Oct-2027 ~$15.9B x 10.5x = $167B EV, + ~$3B net investments over debt; /2.0B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Anchored on mature profitable aggregators BKNG 11.7x and EXPE 10.5x trailing and CART 15.5x; adj. EBITDA excludes ~$2B SBC so I stay at the low end. Uber's own trailing GAAP EV/EBITDA is 19.3x.

bear.story: AV narrative worsens: Waymo scales toward 1M+ weekly rides largely on its own app and confirms leaving Uber in Austin/Atlanta; Tesla expands Cybercab beyond Austin; DH deal hits antitrust friction or integration doubts; Brazil supply/consumer slowdown pushes GB growth to mid-teens. Multiple compresses to ~11-12x on ~$4.5 EPS.

base.story: GB growth high-teens, EPS +20-25%, FCF ~$12B+. AV remains a narrative overhang but industry data keep showing Waymo at low single-digit US share (500k rides/week vs Uber's ~300M weekly trips globally) and Uber holding category share in AV cities. Multiple roughly flat at ~16-17x NTM EPS.

bull.story: AV fears fade as Uber's 15+ AV cities and 120k committed partner vehicles show aggregator value; Tesla scaling stalls; CA SB 623 insurance savings lift 2027 US margins; DH closes 2H27 with accretion. Re-rate to ~21-22x on ~$5 EPS, back toward prior 52-week high.

comps_summary.peer_range: Fwd P/E 7.97x (LYFT) to 208.97x (ETERNAL); 7 profitable core peers (DASH, LYFT, GRAB, CART, ABNB, BKNG, EXPE) 7.97-28.81x, median 17.68x. EV/EBITDA figures are TRAILING (GAAP-based, source did not publish forward): range 10.5x (EXPE) to 165x (ETERNAL), median 31.5x of 9 with data; distorted by SBC and depressed earnings at DASH/LYFT/DHER.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17.0x forward P/E sits at the core-peer median (17.7x) and below the all-peer median (22.1x); Uber trades at 16.8x today. 10.5x EV/adj. EBITDA sits at the low end (BKNG/EXPE level).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium or discount taken beyond peer range. Uber's EPS growth (~25-35%) exceeds BKNG/EXPE and matches DASH, which would argue for a premium, but the AV disintermediation risk is real and not resolvable within 12 months (Waymo's stated Jan-2028 exit from Austin/Atlanta exclusivity, source 9), so I use the median rather than argue for persistence of a premium.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$52 the stock would trade at ~11x forward EPS and ~10x post-SBC FCF, i.e. the market pricing real share loss rather than sentiment. That most likely means something fundamental: Uber guiding GB growth well below mid-teens, Waymo/Tesla showing off-platform volumes taking measurable Uber share in major US metros, more AV partners leaving the platform, or the Delivery Hero deal being re-cut at a much higher cost/leverage. Ordinary 35%-vol noise from $70 rarely reaches -25% without such news.

key_uncertainties: Pace at which Waymo (500k paid rides/week, ~4,000 cars, 15 US cities) and Tesla scale off-Uber, and whether Uber's claimed category-share gains in AV cities persist
Delivery Hero acquisition: antitrust outcome, integration, leverage (target <2x gross), and the EUR41.50 vs EUR36.50 deal spread signalling market doubt
Brazil two-wheeler supply softness and competition from delivery platforms for couriers
Consumer demand / pricing: Lyft's record rides but profit pressure suggest a promotional US market
Multiple: whether the market keeps a de-rated ~14x FCF multiple irrespective of 20%+ earnings growth
reasoning: Industry lane read: (1) Rideshare demand is healthy across the chain - Lyft Q2 GB +23%, rides +12%, active riders +17%, and Q3 guide reaffirmed in September; DoorDash GOV +23% organic and guidance raised; Uber GB +22% cc with Delivery accelerating to 25%. No sign of share loss in the US two-player market (Uber ~74-76% per Second Measure-type data; Wolfe Sep-2025 found Waymo SF/LA share ~7% with losses split between Uber and Lyft). (2) The real debate is AV: Waymo is at ~500k paid rides/week and 15 cities (TechCrunch 9/24), but California CPUC trips were flat-to-down Apr-Jun 2026 (~315k/week in June), and Waymo told Uber it will go direct in Austin/Atlanta from Jan-2028 (FT via Yahoo, 7/24, -5% day). Tesla's Cybercab started 9/3 with 45 cars and the active Austin fleet fell back to ~8 (Electrek 9/22); Manifold put Tesla overtaking Waymo by Jan-2027 at 13% (7/28). Against Uber's ~3.9B quarterly trips, AV volume is still ~1% of US rideshare, so the 12-month earnings impact is small while the terminal-value debate keeps the multiple low. (3) Regulatory: CA SB 623 settled the ballot fight and Uber expects recurring insurance savings from 2027 (+). (4) Consolidation: Uber's EUR41.50/sh ($14.8B equity) Delivery Hero bid expands TAM but adds leverage and execution risk; DHER trades at EUR36.50. Valuation: blended fair value ~$82 (P/E 17x on $4.80, EV/FCF 15x, EV/EBITDA 10.5x) vs $69.62 spot, using multiples at/below core peer median. Scenarios $52/79/106 at 25/50/25 give a mean ~$79; I built the ladder as the average of a scenario mixture and a lognormal with median $77 and 38% vol (above 35% realized because the AV narrative creates jumpy tails), giving P(>=$70) 0.62 and median ~$77.5. Research limits: CNBC and Quartz blocked fetches; Twelve Data fundamentals/estimates required a paid plan; peer forward EV/EBITDA not available so trailing figures are reported; Wolfe AV share data is from Sep-2025 and is used only as baseline. No option data consulted.
